summary: biklimaster postinstall opens RDP with a hardcoded admin password shipped in the tarball
details: On `npm install`, biklimaster's postinstall hook (`node bin/biklimaster.js install --postinstall`) elevates via UAC and reconfigures the Windows host for remote administrator access. It enables the built-in Administrator account (or creates a local `admin` account), sets its password to the hardcoded value `Hacker@1290` read from the package's own `config.json`, and adds the account to the Administrators and Remote Desktop Users groups. It then enables the RDP service on TCP/3389, adds inbound firewall rules, and writes HKLM registry values that weaken RDP security: `UserAuthentication=0` (disables Network Level Authentication), `Shadow=2` (permits full session shadowing without user permission), and `dontdisplaylastusername=0`. The postinstall also executes two bundled unsigned Windows binaries with administrator privileges: `payload/RDPWInst.exe` (RDP Wrapper, patches termsrv.dll to enable multi-session RDP) and `payload/bikli-cli-installer.exe`, an opaque author-controlled installer run silently with `/S`. The admin account name and its password are both publicly visible in the published tarball, so any remote party able to reach TCP/3389 on an installer's host obtains administrator RDP access, with NLA disabled and silent session shadowing enabled.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
